newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices firmer, lists abound.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices firmer, lists abound.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were about two basis points firmer by midday following a wave of morning bid lists that included several blocks from a single arbitrageur.

"There was a slew of index bonds that were out for the bid this morning earlier, really before the Philly Fed Survey came out and most of the bids were an 01 to an 02 higher than last night's close," one trader said. "It was one particular arb actually who put all the bonds out for the bid, then a couple of other people jumped on the bandwagon (and) put a few things out for the bid."
The arb had six or seven blocks out, "but didn't trade any of them," the trader said.

"I think the Street in general is upset with the fact that none of the bonds traded and he wasted everybody's time by popping them out for the bid," he said. "Basically the bid side was an 02 higher than last night's close, but he decided not to hit the bid, I don't know why."
Another trader also cited are large amount of lists.
"It hit us all at once," the trader said. "Street-wise there's certainly $125 million, and then customer-wise there's just a lot of stuff coming out."

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was up 19/32 at 97-31/32 to yield 6.66 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract was up 13/32 at 115-11/32. The March T-bond contract was up 16/32 at 112-18/32. The MOB spread was 89 ticks. The December muni contract expires Thursday.

On the economic front, the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Thursday said its diffusion index of business activity in the manufacturing sector fell to -2.2 in December from 6.4 in November. Forecast called for 7.4.
"Actually, the Philly Fed survey was very, very bullish, very constructive, and the market tried to do better, but munis kind of ran out of steam," a trader said.
